Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_Wyll_SD_HavenRomance_ROM.json: The scene takes place in Act 2 camp with Wyll — a traveling companion and possible romance partner — practicing an imaginary courtly dance and inviting the player into an intimate, cinematic duet that can end in kisses. Off‑screen the rest of the party and camp business (Shadowheart, Halsin, Withers/Jergal, debts, temple crises, etc.) may be present but aren’t central to this moment. If the player is on the Dark Urge path, they carry a darker off‑screen history (memory loss, Bhaal‑touched violence, and the reappearance of their gothic servant Sceleritas) that can tint interactions even if it isn’t mentioned in the dance. Wyll’s lines are flirtatious and earnest — he leans into old‑fashioned romance and leaves the choice to the player to accept, decline, or deepen the connection.
- CAMP_Wyll_CRD_Act3Romance_ROM.json: Wyll is a party companion (“the Blade”) with a fraught past — a devilish pact, a difficult relationship with his father, and recent confrontations tied to Mizora and the Ravengard/Lower City events. In Act 3 he asks the player to a private, romantic moment beside the Chionthar under the ancient Wilden Oak, offering a supposedly “wishing” acorn and a vow of lasting love. The scene follows from prior story beats (meeting Mizora, possible raids or arrests around Ravengard) that may already have affected Wyll emotionally, but here he asks to pause those troubles “for a toll of the bell.” Player responses in the samples range from hesitant to wholehearted acceptance or playful banter; the exchange culminates in Wyll kneeling and proposing a shared future.
- CAMP_GoblinHuntTieflingCelebration_CRD_Wyll.json: After the party, this companion is still trying to come down from all the energy, and with a good enough bond it is possible for the player avatar to flirt and unlock a romance option. For Wyll, you cannot romance if you have not learned about Mizora. He is enjoying himself, it would seem, and toasts you as you approach.

retrieved_synopses: The scene takes place in Act 2 camp with Wyll — a traveling companion and possible romance partner — practicing an imaginary courtly dance and inviting the player into an intimate, cinematic duet that can end in kisses. Off‑screen the rest of the party and camp business (Shadowheart, Halsin, Withers/Jergal, debts, temple crises, etc.) may be present but aren’t central to this moment. If the player is on the Dark Urge path, they carry a darker off‑screen history (memory loss, Bhaal‑touched violence, and the reappearance of their gothic servant Sceleritas) that can tint interactions even if it isn’t mentioned in the dance. Wyll’s lines are flirtatious and earnest — he leans into old‑fashioned romance and leaves the choice to the player to accept, decline, or deepen the connection.

Wyll is a party companion (“the Blade”) with a fraught past — a devilish pact, a difficult relationship with his father, and recent confrontations tied to Mizora and the Ravengard/Lower City events. In Act 3 he asks the player to a private, romantic moment beside the Chionthar under the ancient Wilden Oak, offering a supposedly “wishing” acorn and a vow of lasting love. The scene follows from prior story beats (meeting Mizora, possible raids or arrests around Ravengard) that may already have affected Wyll emotionally, but here he asks to pause those troubles “for a toll of the bell.” Player responses in the samples range from hesitant to wholehearted acceptance or playful banter; the exchange culminates in Wyll kneeling and proposing a shared future.

After the party, this companion is still trying to come down from all the energy, and with a good enough bond it is possible for the player avatar to flirt and unlock a romance option. For Wyll, you cannot romance if you have not learned about Mizora. He is enjoying himself, it would seem, and toasts you as you approach.

context: This takes place in the Act 2 camp with Wyll — a traveling companion who can be romanced — caught practicing an imaginary, courtly dance and inviting the player into a private, cinematic duet that can culminate in kisses. The rest of the party and ongoing camp business (other companions, debts, temple crises, etc.) exist off‑screen but aren’t central to this scene.
